Topic: WhatsApp is testing a scam-spotting AI that never reads your chats
Caption Notes: WhatsApp is trialling a feature called Scam Alert. If someone outside your contacts messages you, a small AI model on your own phone checks the message against known scam patterns — nothing is sent to WhatsApp or Meta to do this. If it looks dodgy, you get a private warning with the option to block, report or carry on. It's an early, limited test, so most people won't see it yet, but it's a sign of where messaging safety is heading. Follow @ainofluff for more plain-English AI safety updates.

Topic: Free ChatGPT now shows ads — here's how it decides what to show you
Caption Notes: If you use the free version of ChatGPT, you might start seeing ads pop up in your chats. OpenAI has switched them on for free users across Europe, and UK users already had them from earlier this year. The ads are picked based on what you're currently asking about, plus your rough location — not your past chats or saved memories. Paid plans stay ad-free. Read the full breakdown on ainofluff.co.uk.

Topic: Google's giving students a free year of AI — plus new study tools in Gemini
Caption Notes: Google has started rolling out new study tools inside Gemini: flashcards, practice quizzes and study plans built from your own notes. Eligible college students in many countries can also get a free year of Google's paid AI plan. If you've got a teenager heading off to college, or fancy trying it yourself, it's worth a look — free tools are still free tools. Follow @ainofluff for more plain-English AI updates.
